stem.text: The function \( g \) is defined by the power series \[ g(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}(x - 3)^{n}}{n \cdot 2^{n}} \] for all real \( x \) for which the series converges.

parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the values of \( x \) for which the series for \( g(x) \) converges absolutely. Give your answer as an open interval.

worked_solution.text: Form the ratio of consecutive terms in absolute value.
Take the limit as n grows.
Set the limit less than 1 and solve.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio of the (n+1)st term to the nth term, (x - 3)^(n+1)/((n+1)2^(n+1)) divided by (x - 3)^n/(n 2^n), or its simplified form n|x - 3|/(2(n+1)), with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of the ratio as |x - 3|/2 with correct limit notation; any simplification error in the limit loses this point.
Resolves |x - 3|/2 < 1 to the two-sided inequality 1 < x < 5 or the interval (1, 5); leaving |x - 3| < 2 unresolved does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Determine whether the series for \( g(x) \) converges at each endpoint of the interval from part (a), and state the interval of convergence of the series. Justify your answers.

worked_solution.text: At x = 5 the series is the alternating harmonic series.
Its terms 1/n decrease to 0, so it converges by the alternating series test.
At x = 1 every term is -1/n, the negative of the harmonic series, which diverges.

points.criterion: Substitutes both x = 1 and x = 5 and writes the two resulting numerical series, the sum of -1/n and the sum of (-1)^(n+1)/n.

Concludes the series at x = 5 converges by the alternating series test and the series at x = 1 diverges as a multiple of the harmonic series (or a p-series with p = 1), and states the interval of convergence 1 < x <= 5.

parts.prompt: The series obtained by differentiating the series for \( g(x) \) term by term is \[ g'(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}(x - 3)^{n-1}}{2^{n}}. \] Find the interval of convergence of this series. Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: Ratio of consecutive terms and its limit.
The series converges absolutely when the limit is less than 1.
At x = 5 the terms are (-1)^(n+1)/2, and at x = 1 every term is 1/2.
Neither sequence of terms tends to 0, so both endpoint series diverge by the nth term test.

points.criterion: Shows the ratio of consecutive terms of the differentiated series and evaluates its limit as |x - 3|/2 with correct limit notation.
Resolves the limit inequality to 1 < x < 5 or the interval (1, 5).
Substitutes both endpoints and writes the two series, the sum of (-1)^(n+1)/2 and the sum of 1/2.
Concludes both endpoint series diverge because their terms do not approach 0 (nth term test), and states the interval of convergence 1 < x < 5.
